title: The に and へ particles
summary: に marks a target of some kind: a destination, a purpose, a place where something is, or what something becomes. へ only copies the destination use.

blocks.text: **に** is a logical particle that marks the **target** of an action. If を is what the action is done to, に is **where it is aimed**. Almost every use of に is a target of some kind.
1. A physical target: where you go

blocks.jp: （私が）さくらにボールを投げた。

blocks.text: 2. A purpose target: why you go
Take the **い-stem** of a verb (it works as a noun for the act) and mark it with に. The place is the physical target; the purpose is the volitional target. One sentence can have both.
店に卵を買いに行く。 (I) go to the shop to buy eggs.

blocks.en: (I) go to the shop to buy eggs.

blocks.text: Being at a place is a target that has already been reached, so に marks the location of existing and being.

blocks.en: The book is on the desk.

blocks.text: The result of a change is a target too. The picture is transformation: A becomes B, and B takes に.

blocks.jp: さくらはカエルになった。
今年（私が）十八歳になる。

blocks.text: An **い-adjective** cannot take に directly (it is an engine, not a carriage). Change **い → く** to get an adverb, and then use なる: 美しい → 美しく**なる**.

blocks.jp: さくらが美しくなった。

blocks.text: **へ** (read "e" as a particle) is a one-trick pony. It repeats only the **destination** use of に (公園へ行く) and can never mark where something stays.

items: **に** marks a **target**: a destination, a purpose, a place where something is, or what something turns into.
い-adjective + なる: **い → く**, then **なる**.
**へ** only marks a **direction of travel**; it cannot mark a location.

questions.note: A destination, purpose, location or result: all targets.

questions.prompt: (I) go to the shop to buy eggs.

questions.note: い-adjectives use く in front of なる.

questions.prompt: へ can mark the place where something stays.
questions.note: へ only marks a direction of travel.
A place where someone is takes に.

questions.instruction: Tap the purpose target (the reason for going)
questions.note: 買い is the い-stem of 買う, used as a noun and marked with に.

questions.prompt: さくらはカエル＿＿なった。

questions.instruction: What is 買い in 買いに行く?
options: The い-stem used as a noun
questions.note: The い-stem names the act, so に can mark it as a purpose.

questions.instruction: Why can an い-adjective not take に directly?
options: It is an engine, not a carriage, so it changes い to く
questions.note: 美しい → 美しく + なる.

questions.instruction: Which means "The book is on the desk"?
questions.note: A location of existing takes に (and ある for things).

questions.instruction: Which sentence has a purpose target?
questions.note: 買いに is the purpose: "go in order to buy".

questions.prompt: 今年（私が）十八歳になる。
questions.note: になる: become. The result, eighteen, is the target.
